title: Unauthorized Transaction, Phishing and Fraud Escalation Policy
content: Any caller reporting unauthorized debits, stolen credentials, phishing, scam calls, or account takeover must be escalated immediately to a live fraud response specialist. Zero-liability protection under RBI guidelines applies when unauthorized electronic transactions are reported promptly within 3 working days. Bank representatives never ask customers to share OTPs, passwords, PINs, CVV codes, or remote screen-sharing access.

title: National Cyber Crime Helpline (1930) and Golden Hour Fraud Reporting
content: Victims of online financial fraud or cyber scams must immediately call the National Cyber Crime Helpline at 1930 or submit a complaint on the official portal at cybercrime.gov.in. Under the 'Golden Hour' protocol, reporting within 2 to 4 hours of unauthorized fund transfer enables law enforcement and the Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting System (CFCFRMS) to freeze illicit funds across intermediary bank accounts before scammers can withdraw cash.

title: Emergency Instant Account Freeze and Debit Suspension Hotline
content: In case of emergency fraud, device loss, or suspected account compromise, customers can immediately freeze all debits without needing internet banking: Call the dedicated 24x7 emergency helpline 1800-425-3800 and press 0, or send an SMS 'FREEZE <Account Number>' to 567676 from your registered mobile number. This freezes all outbound UPI, ATM withdrawals, NetBanking debits, and card swipes instantly.

title: RBI Customer Protection Liability Framework for Unauthorized Electronic Debits
content: Under RBI Circular DBR.No.Leg.BC.78/09.07.005/2017-18: 1. Zero Liability: If the customer notifies the bank within 3 working days of receiving unauthorized transaction alert, customer liability is zero. 2. Limited Liability: If reported between 4 to 7 working days, customer liability is capped at ₹5,000 for basic savings and ₹10,000 for other savings accounts. 3. Bank must credit the shadow/provisional reversal to the customer account within 10 working days.

title: Remote Desktop App Scams (AnyDesk, TeamViewer, RustDesk) Advisory
content: Scammers pose as bank executives, courier agents, or utility officers and trick victims into installing remote desktop applications such as AnyDesk, TeamViewer QuickSupport, or RustDesk. Once installed, the scammer views the phone screen, captures OTPs, and drains bank accounts. Bank advisory: The bank will NEVER ask you to download any screen sharing or remote management tool. Never grant accessibility permissions to unknown apps.

title: Fake Electricity Bill Disconnection and SIM KYC SMS Scams
content: Fraudsters circulate alarming SMS messages claiming 'Your electricity bill is unpaid; power will be disconnected tonight at 9:30 PM. Call officer immediately' or 'Your SIM card KYC is expired'. Calling the number leads to demands for a ₹10 recharge via a malicious link that steals debit card or netbanking credentials. Real utility companies never send urgent disconnection threats requesting APK downloads or third-party money transfers.

title: SIM Swap Fraud Indicators and Immediate Preventive Measures
content: SIM Swap fraud occurs when a criminal obtains a duplicate SIM card of your registered mobile number using forged documents to intercept one-time passwords (OTPs). Warning Signs: If your phone suddenly loses cellular network connectivity and shows 'No Service' or 'SOS' in areas with known good coverage, you may be experiencing a SIM swap. Action: Immediately contact your mobile operator from another phone and freeze your bank account.

title: Phishing Websites, Fake Banking APK Files, and Malware Protection
content: Cybercriminals distribute malicious Android Package (APK) files via WhatsApp or SMS, impersonating official bank rewards, free loan approvals, or PM schemes. Once installed, these APKs intercept SMS OTPs and transmit banking keystrokes. Safeguards: Always download banking applications only from official app stores (Google Play Store or Apple App Store); verify developer credentials and never sideload APKs from unknown links.

title: ATM Skimming Countermeasures and PIN Pad Shielding Rules
content: ATM skimming involves hidden magnetic strip card readers and pinhole cameras placed on automated teller machines. Protection Rules: 1. Inspect the card reader slot; if it feels loose, misaligned, or unusually bulky, do not use the ATM and notify security. 2. Always shield the PIN keypad with your free hand while entering your 4-digit PIN to block hidden cameras. 3. Prefer bank branch ATMs with security guards over isolated off-site kiosks.

title: Aadhaar Biometric Locking via mAadhaar to Prevent AePS Fraud
content: To prevent unauthorized biometric withdrawals via Aadhaar Enabled Payment System (AePS), account holders are strongly advised to lock their Aadhaar biometrics using the official UIDAI website or the mAadhaar smartphone application. Once locked, fingerprint and iris scans cannot be authenticated for financial transactions. Biometrics can be temporarily unlocked for 10 minutes when required for legitimate branch visits or Video KYC.

title: Card CVV Protection and Safe Merchant Swiping Guidelines
content: The 3-digit Card Verification Value (CVV) printed on the back of your debit or credit card is vital for online transactions. Safety best practice: Memorize your CVV number and obscure or scratch it off the physical plastic card with a marker or sticker. When dining out or shopping, never allow a waiter or cashier to take your card out of your sight. Insist on the POS terminal being brought to your table.

title: Part-Time Job, YouTube Video Liking, and Crypto Investment Scams
content: Scammers contact victims via WhatsApp or Telegram offering ₹500 to ₹3,000 per day for simple tasks like liking YouTube videos, writing fake Google reviews, or hotel ratings. After paying small initial rewards to build trust, victims are lured into 'prepaid crypto trading tasks' and coerced into depositing lakhs of rupees. Advisory: Legitimate companies never demand money or deposit fees to release earnings.

title: Identity Theft Prevention, PAN Misuse, and Credit Bureau Auditing
content: Identity theft occurs when fraudsters use stolen copies of your PAN card and Aadhaar card to obtain fraudulent instant loans or credit cards. Protection: Check your official free annual credit report from CIBIL, Experian, or CRIF High Mark every 6 months to ensure no unauthorized loan accounts exist. If unfamiliar loan accounts appear, report identity theft to the issuing institution and the cyber police immediately.

title: Public Wi-Fi Risks and Secure Internet Banking Connection Protocol
content: Free public Wi-Fi networks in airports, railway stations, and coffee shops are frequently unencrypted and vulnerable to Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) packet sniffing and DNS spoofing. Security Rule: Never log in to Internet Banking, Mobile Banking, or enter card details over open public Wi-Fi. Always use cellular mobile data or a trusted personal hotspot. Check for the secure padlock icon and verify the HTTPS URL.

title: Bank Cyber Fraud Investigation Timelines and Provisional Credit SLA
content: Upon receipt of an unauthorized transaction complaint, the bank fraud monitoring cell initiates forensic investigation. In cases where the customer reported within 3 days without negligence, the bank must provide provisional credit (shadow balance) to the customer's account within 10 working days. The final resolution and permanent credit must be completed within 90 days of complaint registration.
